dossier.purpose: Pretrained multilingual text-embedding checkpoint from NVIDIA (Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16): about 1.14B parameters, BF16 safetensors, 2048-dimensional output, 32,768-token maximum input, 34 natural languages, asymmetric 'query:' / 'passage:' prefixes. It turns text into dense vectors for retrieval, semantic search and RAG. It is model weights plus a model card only. No index, vector store, chunker, query CLI, MCP server or agent-client (Claude Code / Codex) integration is part of it, so a caller must chunk text, store vectors, persist state and run the search. It can be loaded with Sentence Transformers, Transformers or vLLM (offline, or as an HTTP embedding server). Release Date on the card: 07/16/2026. Only the Hugging Face model-card page was available (no source repository), so every code-level field below comes from the card's snippets and prose. Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (Model Overview, Description, Release Date, Usage).

claims.claim: Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 is 'a versatile text embedding model trained by NVIDIA and optimized for retrieval and semantic similarity tasks'; it generates 'dense vector embeddings from multilingual text inputs, enabling retrieval, semantic search, and (agentic) RAG workflows'.
'This model is ready for commercial use.'

Use case: 'Most suitable for users who want to build a multilingual question-and-answer application over a large text corpus, leveraging the latest dense retrieval technologies.' Deployment Geography: Global.

Architecture: Transformer encoder with bidirectional attention masking; Network Architecture 'Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512 based pruned model'; approximately 1.14B parameters; hidden size 2048; average pooling over token-level representations; dense embedding of dimension 2048.
Input limit: 'The model's max sequence length is 32768.' Longer inputs 'should be chunked or truncated'.
claims.citation: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (Input(s); Ethical Considerations > Explainability, Technical Limitations & Mitigation)

claims.claim: Asymmetric prefixes: 'Add the query: prefix for queries and the passage: prefix for documents.' On vLLM's /v2/embed endpoint raw strings plus input_type ('query' or 'document') apply the saved prompts automatically; the OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint needs strings in `input` prefixed manually with query: or passage:.

Embeddings are L2-normalized (dot product equals cosine similarity). 'It also supports dynamic embedding sizes by slicing the vector from the start (for example, keeping the first 1024 or 512 dimensions)', provided the sub-vector is re-normalized (L2) after slicing.

34 languages: English, Arabic, Assamese, Bengali, Bulgarian, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, German, Hindi, Hinglish, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Marathi, Nepali, Norwegian, Persian, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Ukrainian, Urdu, Vietnamese. The list contains natural languages only; no programming languages are listed.

Training data: '8.5M+' data points across '161 dataset files' (hybrid human / automated / synthetic). The Public Datasets table includes code-related sets (coir_apps, coir_cosqa, coir_stackoverflow_qa, coir_codetrans_dl, coir_codetrans_contest, synthetic_text2sql, SWE-bench). Synthetic queries / QA pairs were generated with Qwen3 family, gemma-4-31B-it, gpt-oss-120b/20b and Nemotron-3 Super/Ultra models.
Reported results, Avg. NDCG@10 at sequence length 4096: RTEB 72.38; ViDoRe-V3 text 57.74; MMTEB (Retrieval) 71.04.

Runtime engines PyTorch and vLLM; supported microarchitectures NVIDIA Ampere, Blackwell, Hopper; supported OS Linux; test hardware A100 80GB and H100 80GB; examples tested in nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.06-py3.

vLLM: 'For BF16, use vllm==0.25.0 for /v2/embed serving.' NVIDIA also validated `vllm serve "$MODEL_ID"` with vllm/vllm-openai:v0.20.0 through v0.24.0. On Hopper and Ada Lovelace GPUs FP8 can be enabled with `--quantization fp8_per_tensor` ('Validated with vLLM 0.25.0 on H100; accuracy matched BF16').

License: 'This model and its associated configuration files are licensed under the OpenMDW License Agreement, version 1.1 (OpenMDW-1.1).' 'ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Apache License, Version 2.0.' 'This project will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use.'
Known limitation: 'This model does not always guarantee to retrieve the correct passage(s) for a given query.'

install.method: pip, local Python (Linux; CUDA-enabled PyTorch required). For non-default CUDA environments the card says to use the PyTorch selector with an extra --index-url.

NVIDIA PyTorch container (the tested environment): do not upgrade Torch inside it, install only the missing packages. The container includes flash-attn; otherwise set attn_implementation to sdpa. The card gives no docker run command.
vLLM OpenAI image tags that NVIDIA says it validated for BF16 `vllm serve`
install.command: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.20.0 through v0.24.0 (tag range only; the page gives no docker run command)

install.method: Start an HTTP embedding server with vLLM (weights are fetched by model id; for a local checkpoint path add --served-model-name)

entry_points.what: SentenceTransformer(MODEL_ID, device='cuda', model_kwargs={'dtype': torch.bfloat16, 'attn_implementation': 'flash_attention_2'}); model.max_seq_length = 32768; encode_query(...) / encode_document(...) (batch_size=8) and model.similarity(...). Query/document prompts are applied by encode_query / encode_document.

AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, padding_side='left') + AutoModel.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, dtype=bfloat16, attn_implementation='flash_attention_2').to('cuda'); manual 'query: ' / 'passage: ' prefixes, masked average pooling and F.normalize(p=2); raises RuntimeError without CUDA.
from vllm import LLM; LLM(model=MODEL_ID).embed(texts, use_tqdm=False) with manual 'query: ' / 'passage: ' prefixes; scores by query_embeddings @ document_embeddings.T.
`vllm serve "$MODEL_ID"` (optional --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000; --served-model-name for a local checkpoint path) exposes the HTTP embedding API.

POST http://localhost:8000/v2/embed with {model, input_type: 'query'|'document', texts, embedding_types: ['float'], truncate: 'END'}; response['embeddings']['float']. The OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings is also available but needs manual query:/passage: prefixes.

code.architecture: No source repository exists in the material; this is a model checkpoint plus model card. Model: Transformer encoder with bidirectional attention masking, 'Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512 based pruned model' (HF metadata base_model mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512; the model-tree widget root shows mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Base-2512 and its relationship labels are ambiguous in the fetched rendering), about 1.14B parameters, hidden size 2048, average pooling over token states, 2048-d output, 32,768-token context. Built in two prune-and-distill rounds: the 3B parent embedding model was pruned to 2B with NVIDIA ModelOpt mcore_minitron Neural Architecture Search (50k in-domain calibration corpus), then distilled from the fine-tuned Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16 teacher with cosine-distance + MSE losses on a multilingual in-domain retrieval blend, and the procedure was repeated to reach 1.14B. Only file named: config.json (keeps rope_parameters.apply_yarn_scaling for vLLM compatibility). Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (Model Architecture; Pruning and Distillation Procedure; Expected Configuration Warning)

risks: Scope: the artifact is model weights only. No index, vector store, chunker, query CLI, MCP server or Claude Code / Codex integration is provided or documented, so chunking, vector storage, scoping and recoverable index state must be built by the caller. The stated use case is multilingual Q&A over a text corpus, not code search. Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (Usage; Use Case; Software Integration)

Platform: documented only for Linux with NVIDIA Ampere / Blackwell / Hopper GPUs (tested on A100 / H100 80GB) and CUDA-enabled PyTorch. macOS, Windows / WSL and CPU-only are not documented, the Sentence Transformers and Transformers snippets hard-require CUDA (FlashAttention-2 with an sdpa fallback), and no VRAM requirement is stated (my arithmetic only: 1.14B params x 2 bytes BF16 is about 2.3 GB for weights alone). Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (Software Integration; Sentence Transformers; Transformers)

Version pinning and compatibility: needs recent libraries (transformers>=5.2.0, sentence-transformers>=5.4.1) and vllm==0.25.0 for /v2/embed; only vllm-openai v0.20.0-v0.24.0 are stated as validated for `vllm serve`. Loading prints an 'expected' rope_parameters warning because apply_yarn_scaling is kept in config.json for vLLM (upstream work tracked in vLLM issue #48621). Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (Local Python Dependencies; vLLM Dependencies; Expected Configuration Warning)

Licensing: OpenMDW-1.1 governs the model and configuration files; Apache-2.0 appears as 'ADDITIONAL INFORMATION' with no stated scope; the network is derived from Mistral's Ministral-3-3B; training used synthetic data from third-party models (Qwen, gemma-4-31B-it, gpt-oss, Nemotron) plus public sets including SWE-bench and CoIR subsets, each with its own terms; the card also warns that setup downloads third-party software under its own licenses. The license text was not opened. Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (License/Terms of Use; Model Architecture; Training Dataset)

Evidence of quality: all published numbers are NVIDIA-reported averages (RTEB, ViDoRe-V3 text, MMTEB retrieval) at sequence length 4096. No code-retrieval benchmark, per-task breakdown, latency / throughput, long-context result or sliced-dimension result is published, the 34-language list contains no programming languages, and the card itself says retrieval 'does not always guarantee' the correct passage. Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (Evaluation Dataset; Model Overview; Explainability)

Security: the card's explicit-bind example runs `vllm serve ... --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` and its request sample uses plain http, with no authentication or TLS guidance. Vulnerability reporting goes through an NVIDIA web form; there is no SECURITY.md. For balance: the weights are Safetensors and no snippet passes trust_remote_code. Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (vLLM Online Serving; Recommended Retrieval Endpoint; Safety)

Maintenance and provenance: no source repository, tag, commit hash, changelog, release workflow, checksums or signatures are shown, so the revision is unpinned and a consumer must pin one itself. The card gives Release Date 07/16/2026 while the collection widget shows 'updated Aug 11'. Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 (Release Date; sidebar widgets)

checks.note: Each part is confirmed by the card's code. Sentence Transformers: SentenceTransformer(MODEL_ID, device='cuda', model_kwargs={dtype: torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation: 'flash_attention_2'}), then encode_query / encode_document (batch_size=8) and model.similarity. Transformers: AutoTokenizer(padding_side='left'), then average_pool (a masked mean over last_hidden_state), then F.normalize(pooled, p=2, dim=-1). vLLM offline: LLM(model=MODEL_ID).embed(texts, use_tqdm=False). HTTP: requests.post to http://localhost:8000/v2/embed with exactly those JSON keys, read via response.json()['embeddings']['float'] and called as embed('query', QUERIES) / embed('document', DOCUMENTS). /v1/embeddings: 'You can also use the OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint. For those requests, pass strings in input and manually prefix them with query: or passage:.' No sample calls /v1/embeddings. Trivial nit: that text is two sentences, not one.

checks.field: claim_checks[0] (code retrieval / code search, verified: partial)
checks.statement: Public Datasets lists coir_apps, coir_cosqa, coir_stackoverflow_qa, coir_codetrans_dl, coir_codetrans_contest, synthetic_text2sql (CoIR-Retrieval links) and SWE-bench; every usage snippet embeds two Python-function documents; no training code/data mix, no code-retrieval benchmark and no per-task results are published; the stated use case is multilingual Q&A over a text corpus, not code search.
checks.note: All seven rows are present. The coir_* and synthetic_text2sql rows link to huggingface.co/datasets/CoIR-Retrieval/... (e.g. /apps, /cosqa, /synthetic-text2sql); SWE-bench links to princeton-nlp/SWE-bench. Each sample redefines QUERIES / DOCUMENTS: two code queries ('Write a Python function that counts...' and 'Write a function that orders a dictionary...') matched with `def frequency_lists` and `def sort_dict_item`, plus two health Q/A pairs. The training data is given only as 'Total Size: 8.5M+ data points; Total Number of Datasets: 161 dataset files', with no per-dataset mix. The results table has only averages for RTEB, ViDoRe-V3 text and MMTEB (Retrieval); there is no code benchmark. The Use Case quote matches. Omission: the sidebar 'Nemotron 3 Embed' collection description says 'Open embedding models for enterprise RAG, agentic retrieval, code search, and agent memory.' That is collection text, not the card body, so 'partial' is still the right rating.
